facts.reason: Source states eukaryotic replication initiates from many sites called replication origins; organism (eukaryotes) and stage (initiation) match.
Passage directly states initiation from origins must be tightly controlled so the entire genome is precisely duplicated each cell cycle. Meaning and scope match.

Passage states control is accomplished by regulating loading and activation of the replicative DNA helicase. Review emphasizes budding-yeast proteins, so broad eukaryotic generalization is an extrapolation of framing, but the stated claim is entailed.

Passage explicitly states the preponderance of evidence supports a model in which Pol ε carries out the bulk of leading-strand synthesis at an undisturbed fork. Claim preserves the model-level hedge and 'undisturbed fork' qualifier.
Passage states Pol α carries out initiation of Okazaki fragment synthesis. The parenthetical 'priming implied' is supported by the role of initiation in this context; no ungrounded extension.
Passage states Pol δ carries out elongation and maturation of Okazaki fragments. Direct role match.
Passage frames the review around enzymes that synthesize DNA and repair discontinuities on the lagging strand of the replication fork. Entailed at the framing level.

Passage discusses alternative proposals including cellular processes during which alternative forks may be utilized, and biochemical reconstitution studies examining leading and lagging synthesis separately and jointly. Claim accurately paraphrases; 'disputed' is a labeling choice but content is entailed. Builder status CONFLICTED is unsupported; no contradicting evidence exists.
Passage states DNA pol can add nucleotides only in the 5' to 3' direction. Extractively sourced; claim matches passage meaning for the stated context. No scene-level scope confirmation.

Passage states once the 3' end of the lagging strand template is sufficiently elongated, DNA polymerase can add nucleotides complementary to chromosome ends. Entailed in telomerase context; note this concerns telomere completion, not general fork synthesis.
Passage states DNA polymerase can add nucleotides in only one direction. Vague but entailed; directionality specified in adjacent passage.

Passage states one strand complementary to the parental strand is synthesized continuously toward the replication fork so polymerase can add nucleotides in this direction. Entailed; leading-strand context.
Passage states because DNA polymerase can only synthesize 5' to 3', the other new strand is made in short pieces called Okazaki fragments. Entailed; lagging-strand context.

Passage describes nucleotide excision repair: double strand unwound/separated, incorrect bases removed with a few flanking bases, replaced by copying template with DNA polymerase. Entailed as stated, but off-topic for the replication-mechanism video; also note textbook conflates RNase H with flap endonuclease elsewhere, so caution on adjacent claims.
Passage states only purine-pyrimidine pairing and antiparallel orientation can explain uniform diameter. Entailed as stated. Off-topic for replication mechanism video.

Passage states ddNTP incorporation prevents further extension because the free 3' OH needed to add another nucleotide is unavailable. Entailed. Off-topic (Sanger sequencing), not replication mechanism.
